prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1357; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states the other vehicle crossed into the lane during a slight curve. No airbag deployment reported. Both vehicles driven from scene. Photos requested from both parties and scene diagram obtained from the insured.

Entry 2: Claimant's vehicle inspected at repair facility. Front bumper cover, radiator support and headlamp assembly show damage consistent with a low-speed impact. Repair estimate received and under review. Police report reviewed; citation issued to the other driver for failure to keep in lane.

Entry 3: Claimant is represented by counsel. Letter of representation received. All further communication to be directed to the attorney's office. Claimant's bodily injury claim noted as neck strain with reported stiffness and headaches. Medical authorization forms requested through counsel.

Entry 4: Records received from claimant's treating chiropractor describing soft tissue neck strain, conservative treatment and a limited range of motion. No imaging ordered at this time. Physical therapy referral noted. File flagged for medical review and reserve adjusted to reflect current treatment plan.

Entry 5: Attorney's demand package received and logged. Demand is under evaluation against medical records, repair invoice and liability findings. Liability assessed as primarily with the other driver. Negotiation scheduled to continue once outstanding bills and treatment notes are received. Diary set for follow-up in 30 days.
